\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পদ} (pôd)}{পদ (pôd)}]{\bn{পদ} (pôd) — a post; a position}

\label{lesson:BN-C496-pod}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a pension, then the Bengali for to be worth it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পদ}}
\textbf{\bn{পদ}} — \emph{pôd} — \textquotedblleft{}a post; a position\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তিনি} \bn{অফিসে} \bn{একটা} \bn{বড়} \bn{পদে} \bn{আছেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tini ôphise ekṭā bôṛo pôde āchhen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She holds a senior post at the office.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পদ}} (\emph{pôd}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{pada}, \textquotedblleft{}a step\textquotedblright{}, and from that \textquotedblleft{}a place, a rank\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Tini ôphise ekṭā bôṛo pôde āchhen.} — She holds a senior post at the office.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a pension, then the Bengali for to be worth it, then say \emph{pôd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পদ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A post; a position\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পদোন্নতি} (pôdonnôti)}{পদোন্নতি (pôdonnôti)}]{\bn{পদোন্নতি} (pôdonnôti) — a promotion}

\label{lesson:BN-C496-podonnoti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to be worth it, then the Bengali for a post at work.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পদোন্নতি}}
\textbf{\bn{পদোন্নতি}} — \emph{pôdonnôti} — \textquotedblleft{}a promotion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুই} \bn{বছর} \bn{পরে} \bn{আমার} \bn{পদোন্নতি} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dui bôchhôr pôre āmār pôdonnôti hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After two years I got a promotion.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পদোন্নতি}} (\emph{pôdonnôti}) joins Sanskrit \emph{pada}, \textquotedblleft{}rank\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{unnati}, \textquotedblleft{}rising, advancement\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): a rise in rank.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôdonnôti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôdonnôti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Dui bôchhôr pôre āmār pôdonnôti hôlô.} — After two years I got a promotion.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to be worth it, then the Bengali for a post at work, then say \emph{pôdonnôti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পদোন্নতি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A promotion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সহকারী} (sôhôkārī)}{সহকারী (sôhôkārī)}]{\bn{সহকারী} (sôhôkārī) — an assistant}

\label{lesson:BN-C496-sohokari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a post at work, then the Bengali for a promotion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সহকারী}}
\textbf{\bn{সহকারী}} — \emph{sôhôkārī} — \textquotedblleft{}an assistant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ম্যানেজারের} \bn{সহকারী} \bn{আমাকে} \bn{ফোন} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mænejārer sôhôkārī āmāke phon kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager's assistant phoned me.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সহকারী}} (\emph{sôhôkārī}) is Sanskrit \emph{sahakārin}, \textquotedblleft{}acting together, co-operating\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): one who works alongside.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a post at work, then the Bengali for a promotion, then say \emph{sôhôkārī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সিনিয়র} (siniyôr)}{সিনিয়র (siniyôr)}]{\bn{সিনিয়র} (siniyôr) — a senior; senior in rank}

\label{lesson:BN-C496-siniyor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a promotion, then the Bengali for an assistant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সিনিয়র}}
\textbf{\bn{সিনিয়র}} — \emph{siniyôr} — \textquotedblleft{}a senior; senior in rank\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{সিনিয়র} \bn{আমাকে} \bn{কাজটা} \bn{বোঝালেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Āmār siniyôr āmāke kājṭā bojhālen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My senior explained the work to me.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সিনিয়র}} (\emph{siniyôr}) is borrowed from English \emph{senior}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকা} (bôhāl thākā)}{বহাল থাকা (bôhāl thākā)}]{\bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকা} (bôhāl thākā) — to stay in post; to remain in force}

\label{lesson:BN-C496-bohal-thaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an assistant, then the Bengali for senior in rank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকা}}
\textbf{\bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকা}} — \emph{bôhāl thākā} — \textquotedblleft{}to stay in post; to remain in force\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{নতুন} \bn{মালিক} \bn{এল}, \bn{কিন্তু} \bn{পুরনো} \bn{ম্যানেজার} \bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nôtun mālik elô, kintu purôno mænejār bôhāl thāklen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A new owner came, but the old manager kept his post.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{পদে} \bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকলেন}, \emph{tini pôde bôhāl thāklen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বহাল} \bn{থাকা}} (\emph{bôhāl thākā}) joins \bn{বহাল}, \textquotedblleft{}in place, in force\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{bahāl}, \textquotedblleft{}restored\textquotedblright{}, to \bn{থাকা}, \textquotedblleft{}to stay\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôhāl thākā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Nôtun mālik elô, kintu purôno mænejār bôhāl thāklen.} — A new owner came, but the old manager kept his post.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an assistant, then the Bengali for senior in rank, then say \emph{bôhāl thākā} again
\end{itemize}
